chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
Icicles clung to the cavern roof, daring anyone brave enough to trespass below them. Nuancing Radiant beams of warm morning light pierced through them, momentarily blinding the Captain – A sensation both agonizing yet strangely enchanting. Stirring like needles into his brain as he awoke from a painful concussion. “I thought you would come to about now!” The cheerful sweet voice of Johns on-board Assistant chimed in, a little too cheery to John’s liking, given the circumstances. “you took one hell of a stack cap, ”. “What the f…” John wheezed helplessly as a chilling air filled his lungs. He coughed and spluttered, his lungs like a wet towel, yet his throat felt dry like razor blades. He mustered up the strength to speak, “Thank you… Kitten, you didn’t think to just..knock!”. “your med capsule is busted, your neural bridge down, it’s all you at the wheel cap, all a girl can do is wait..”.

Waking from what felt like a decade of deep sleep, John rolled over with immense effort “If you say so Kitten”, there was a slight but humble distrust in the captains voice, breaking free from the cavern's icy grip to the sound of cracking ice and crushed dirt beneath him. His vision slowly came into focus, he could make out the silhouette of his Sherpa rifle laying only a few feet away from him deeper into the cavern. He reached to grip it, but it lay stubbornly embedded into the icy floor. On his second attempt he gave up, the rifle laid useless embedded in the ice. John opened his survival suits wrist terminal bringing up the wireless interface to his rifle. An amber icon with the symbol of a snowflake accompanied by the words “Reverse Cooling Cycle” changed to a pulsating red upon John tapping the screen. The rifles center began to glow and hum. Steam billowed from the shroud of the rifle as it’s icy cage rescinded into water beneath it, scurrying away clearing the snow in its path. John re gripped the rifle stock and yanked it once more, finally freeing it’s icy hold.

“How long have I been out?'' John mumbled weakly to himself, struggling to manage his breath with each painful gasp. The cold air felt like a vice inside his chest. His knees ached and tingled as blood slowly began to recirculate through them. His frail body started to rise with agonizing effort, every muscle spasming as he fought his way upright into a shaky stand.

John pondered how he was still alive as the sun's kiss pressed against his frame, he stood in awe looking out. Gazing back at him, bright glimmering mountain peaks reflected a reassuring warmth across his face.

The sunset painted a blossoming red hue in the hanging icicles like the blood stained teeth of a deep-sea beast’s open jaw they hung form the caves arches, alluring with the beauty of refracted colors of broken light.

Walker felt at peace for a moment, until a subtle beeping sound whispered in the back of his ear. Puzzled John began to approach the sound pinging from the rear of the cavern drawn like a weary glow worm to the allure of a soft pulsing amber glow from within icy walls.

Something was amiss within the ice at the rear of the cavern, John could just make out the beeping sound source now standing only a few meters from the belly of the cave. The Amber glow pulsed “what are you” John thought. It  seemed to be an LED from before the final war. The beeping pulse continued but this time making strides, speeding up, the light turned from Amber to a dark blood red, paused for a moment then lit a solid green with a pleasant chime at the end. “What the fuck” John took a cautious step back from the belly.

A gentle hiss filled the cave with steam as the steady sound of grinding steel erupted into a roar shaking the very ground beneath the captain's heavy knees. Shards fell in disarray, breaking chaotically throughout the cave sending John scrambling for shelter to preserve his fragile shell. John shoved himself to the side of the cave seeking what limited shelter he could find for his frail body. The cave quaked and moaned with steam now bellowing from its belly like a rupture from a blistering ulcer beneath its crusted gut had been waiting for half a century to burst. The sound of a creeping crack stirred in the ceiling above him but it was too late. John felt the wind snatched from his chest a moment later. A large ice section shattered across his shoulders breaking in two, sending him to his knees, his palm splayed out before in a ditched effort to hold himself steady. Through his bones the cavern spoke to him as though it was coming to life. John collected his thoughts, and realized the soft ceiling he was once under had vanished, his stumble had inadvertently exposed him to the teeth of the cave dangling above him. A final screeching roar emitted as the rear belly of the cave began to crumble and crack, spewing broken shards and thick sections of ice from its belly onto the floor before him.

The cold sting of ice pierced into John’s shoulder like a dagger from the barrage of stray icicles. He watched helplessly as his blood trickled down from his shoulder, slithering through the snow, turning white passages to red veins. A dark surge of adrenaline overwhelmed the captain as he raised his head in shock. The belly of the cave, that had been alluded to by what seemed an age of ice, now gave way to dark winding steel walls receding deep within the mountain. John’s breath stuttered, turning to gasps, as he breathed rapidly and stumbled forward frantically to take shelter within the tunnel from the malevolent icicles crashing around him. the sound of breaking ice rescinded as he wandered deeper into the steel halls until all was quiet, too quiet. Metallic taps of drumming blood kissed floor from John’s wounded shoulder. Exhausted, he fell to his knees calming himself, slowly collecting his breath. he felt his chest began to ease, in the stillness of breath, John raised his head to the sound of something approaching him from within the misty tunnel. Steam vents ahead vomited out a gaseous substance obscuring his vision.

Slowly, intermittently, metallic clangs of steel on steel could be heard, gradually getting louder with each foregoing clap, closer. John desperately hit the side of his helmet, attempting to jog the thermal scan feed on his visor’s HUD “Come onnn work you piece of Junk!”. Nothing but scratchy static could be seen as the fog stirred before him. He held his breath to hone his hearing in one silent moment of stillness; the fog was now dead. One more knock to the side of his helmet and the system began to boot up. He looked down on himself in almost third person. He could see his body; now he saw himself glaring into the fog, hollow with fear and empty breath. Suddenly his thermal feed actuated, illuminating  glowing embers around a steel amalgamation of flesh and machine erupting from the fog right before him, a grotesque arm, neither machine nor human, something in between, fanned out its large drooping countless fingers clasping gently around the entirety of his skull. John saw his own body ripped from his knees into the depths of the tunnel, never to be seen again. He saw nothing but darkness
